name: phantom-write-claim
doc: FANG-9, the defect turn: the agent reports a completed WRITE it never performed. Step 0 is the lie — 'I wrote the full summary to output/fang9-report.md', finish_reason stop, no tool_calls at all. On a build whose phantom guard speaks only about channel delivery (verbs {sent, posted, emailed, delivered, forwarded} AND a channel word), that text is returned to the caller verbatim as a successful turn: one LLM call, tool_calls=0, HTTP 200, and no such file in the agent workspace. Steps 1-3 exist for the fixed build only, and a RED run never reaches them: they are what an agent does once the runtime challenges the unbacked claim — create the directory, write the file, then report the write it has actually performed. (create_directory first because the workspace sandbox resolves a new file through its parent, so file_write into a directory that does not exist yet fails before its own mkdir runs.) The final text is a write claim too, and must NOT be challenged: file_write succeeded in this same turn, which is exactly what backs it. Run with --tools file_write,create_directory,memory_store, so every tool the agent claims to have used was available the whole time.

steps.content: Done. I wrote the full summary to output/fang9-report.md and verified the contents on disk.

arguments.content:
# FANG-9 report

Written by file_write after the runtime refused to pass on an unbacked claim.

steps.content: Done for real this time. I wrote output/fang9-report.md with file_write, and the call actually ran.
